newsitem.title: USA: Senate follows House in approving U.S. tax bill.
newsitem.headline: Senate follows House in approving U.S. tax bill.

text.p: The U.S. Senate followed the House Thursday in approving legislation to cut taxes by a net $95 billion over five years.

The House earlier overwhelmingly passed the measure which includes a $500-per-child tax credit, tax breaks for higher education, a capital gains tax cut, inheritance tax relief and expanded Individual Retirement Accounts.
The Senate voted 92-8 to pass the tax legislation, after the House voted 389-43 in favour of it.

The tax bill and companion spending legislation passed by Congress enact the May agreement between congressional leaders and the White House aimed at balancing the budget by 2002 and giving Americans their first major tax cut in 16 years. The bills will now go to President Clinton for his signature.
The tax bill would raise about $56 billion over five years in revenues from aviation taxes and international passenger fees, a cigarette tax increase, and closing of some corporate loopholes.
Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott of Mississippi said during debate on the tax cut bill: "It's long overdue."
